clue.text: Plays safe, in both senses, playing side

indicators.note: in says the word for side is set inside the shuffled letters
playing here means toying with the letters of both senses until they fall into a new order

parts.note: an edge is a side or border

explanation.surface: A cautious football manager plays safe with both his team and his options, putting out a defensive side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in both senses' looks like a comment on the definition; really 'in' places EDGE inside HSONESBETS, the reworking of BOTH SENSES that 'playing' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to protect yourself by backing more than one outcome is to play it safe.

clue.text: Prisoner who was 90 kept in a very long time

indicators.note: kept in says the Roman number is held inside the word for an age

parts.note: an eon is an immensely long period
XC is 90 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An old prisoner of ninety has been locked up for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A former convict is someone who once served time in jail.

clue.text: Supporter's Liverpool kit returned

indicators.note: returned says the joined words are sent back, read from the end

parts.note: Liverpool FC play in red and are nicknamed the Reds
a rig is an outfit, kit

explanation.surface: A Liverpool fan sends back his replica football kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan but is a structural beam; the 's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: A girder is a large beam that holds up a structure, a supporter in the engineering sense.

clue.text: Son's emotional film about football match one loved

indicators.note: about says the word for a tearjerker goes round the word for a match

parts.note: a weepie is a sentimental film
a tie is a cup match in football

explanation.surface: A son's tearjerker of a film is about a football game.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment for a darling, someone dearly loved.

clue.text: Puts head on floor, standing upside-down

indicators.note: standing upside-down in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to floor someone is to stun them

explanation.surface: Someone does a headstand, putting their head on the floor upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To nut someone is British slang for headbutting them.

clue.text: Man of the match?

definitions.meaning: a forward player in football, the team's goalscorer
someone who strikes a match to light it

explanation.surface: Who was the player of the game?
explanation.definitionFit: Both a football forward and one who ignites a matchstick fit the description.

clue.text: A club fixer's heading off to develop one of our team

indicators.note: to develop means to evolve, so these letters change into a new form
heading off says the first letter of fixer is dropped

explanation.surface: A club's match-fixer leaves to develop a player in the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our team' is the panel of Telegraph Toughie setters, which includes one called Excalibur.
explanation.definitionFit: Excalibur is the pseudonym of a fellow setter of Telegraph Toughie puzzles, so a team member.

clue.text: One charged in report about club post-season?

indicators.note: about says the report surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a story is a news report

indicators.note: post means after, so the word for club follows the word for season

parts.note: to age wine or wood is to season it
to batter is to club, beat

explanation.surface: A player is accused in a report about his club after the season ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An accumulator holds electrical energy, so it is something charged up rather than accused.

clue.text: Kick the ball — hack — in due direction

indicators.note: in says the kick and the hack sit within the word for due

parts.note: coming means due, about to arrive
to pass is to kick the ball to a team-mate
to hack something is to bear or tolerate it

explanation.surface: A defender kicks the ball and hacks at an opponent in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearing taken with a magnetic needle is the heading or line of travel.

clue.text: Heads for opening ceremony — now what's happening?

indicators.note: the heads of the two words opening and ceremony are their first letters

parts.note: current means present, of now

explanation.surface: The start of an opening ceremony leaves someone asking what is going on now.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurrent is a formal adjective for something taking place at the moment, an event in progress.

clue.text: Answer? There's no answer, and nothing on page

indicators.note: on says the zero goes on after the shortened word
there's no says one letter is missing from the word for respond

parts.note: to react is to answer or respond
to react is to answer or respond
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader asks for an answer and finds a blank page.
explanation.walkthrough: REACT loses its A to leave RECT, then O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A recto is the right-hand page of an open book, so a particular kind of leaf side.

clue.text: Incisive information used in bet

indicators.note: used in says the word for information is placed within the word for bet

parts.note: a punt is a wager
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Sharp inside information is put to use in placing a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent remarks are sharp and biting, the same quality as incisive comment.

clue.text: Is upset about fine backing for drinking songs

indicators.note: backing says the whole assembly is read from right to left
about says the word for unwell goes round the word for fine

parts.note: someone who ails is unwell, upset in the stomach
OK means fine

explanation.surface: Someone is upset about a fine and drinks to forget, singing as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the reversal signal, but here 'Is upset' means being unwell; 'about' wraps it round the word for fine, and 'backing' turns the result into AILOKS read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Skolia were ancient Greek songs sung in turn by guests at a banquet, so songs for drinking.

clue.text: Get to catch mostly very good football film

indicators.note: to catch says the word for get grabs the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to fetch is to go and get

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of very is lost

parts.note: pi is short for pious, good

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to see a very good football film.
explanation.definitionFit: Fever Pitch is a 1997 British film from Nick Hornby's book about an Arsenal fan.

clue.text: Those first to score inclined to exploit this position

indicators.note: the first letters of the next four words, score, inclined, to and exploit, are those picked

explanation.surface: Strikers keen to score early look for the right spot on the pitch to exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or location, the position where something is.

clue.text: Football score that hurts Germany, community gathers

indicators.note: gathers says the community takes in the cry and the country code

parts.note: a town is a community
ouch is the cry of something that hurts
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A goal that pains the German team while the town turns out to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: In American football a touchdown is the main scoring play, worth six points.

clue.text: Clear goal apart from, on review, being bitten by footballer

indicators.note: being bitten by says the footballer's name closes round the other pieces like jaws

parts.note: Pele is the great Brazilian footballer
the net is the goal in football

indicators.note: on review says the word for apart from is looked at backwards

parts.note: bar means except, apart from

explanation.surface: A goal is cleared on video review after a player is bitten by an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on review' turns only the word for 'apart from' backwards, giving RAB; Pele is the Brazilian great whose name does the biting.
explanation.definitionFit: Penetrable means able to be passed through, so a way through is clear.

clue.text: Is attacker L Suarez bit to be replaced?

indicators.note: to be replaced says these letters are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: After Luis Suarez bit an opponent at the 2014 World Cup, people asked whether he should be dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: Suarez was banned for biting Giorgio Chiellini at the 2014 World Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brutalizes treats others savagely, acting as a violent assailant.

clue.text: Slightly upset, reserves given strip

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the letters are turned upside down

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
to rifle a place is to strip it of valuables

explanation.surface: The reserve players are a bit upset to be handed their kit.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be a little or somewhat, as in a mild degree.

clue.text: Quiet way to drop dead — that shows craft

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, quiet

indicators.note: to drop says one letter is let fall from the word for way

parts.note: a road is a way

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a peaceful way to die, which reveals real skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A proa is a Malay sailing boat, so a vessel or craft.

clue.text: Artist fighting depression when energy's gone

parts.note: war is fighting

indicators.note: gone says one letter is taken away from the hollow

parts.note: a hole is a hollow, a depression
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A painter battles depression once his energy is spent.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Warhol was the American pop artist known for soup can prints.

clue.text: Be a defender producing poor header

indicators.note: poor suggests a badly made header whose letters go astray

explanation.surface: A defender makes a poor header and concedes.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere to a cause or person is to stick by them as a supporter, defending it.

clue.text: Feign injury perhaps, with agreement to hold position

indicators.note: to hold says the word for agreement wraps round the word for position

parts.note: a pact is an agreement
lay as a noun means position or arrangement, as in the lay of the land

explanation.surface: A footballer fakes an injury to keep his team's position, with a mutual understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigning injury is an example of pretence, putting on an act to deceive.

clue.text: Extremely awful strike, nearly a record

indicators.note: extremely picks the two extreme letters of awful
nearly says the word for strike is cut short by one letter

parts.note: to bump is to strike

explanation.surface: A dreadful strike almost breaks a record.
explanation.definitionFit: An LP is a long-playing disc, a recording collection.

clue.text: Earache for sandwiches one prepares for restaurant

indicators.note: sandwiches says the answer is held between the letters of earache for

explanation.surface: Someone with an earache makes sandwiches for a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook is the person who makes food in a restaurant kitchen.

clue.text: Losing Hazard contributes to pain of fans

indicators.note: contributes to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Chelsea forward Eden Hazard losing a match adds to the fans' misery.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazard looks like the Chelsea footballer Eden Hazard; in billiards a losing hazard is a shot where the cue ball goes into a pocket off another ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards a losing hazard is the stroke where the cue ball rebounds off the object ball into a pocket.

clue.text: Go for some shots, maybe, and almost score

definitions.meaning: to go to the pub counter to buy drinks such as shots
in football, a shot that strikes the crossbar comes close to a goal

explanation.surface: A striker shoots and nearly scores.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both heading to the pub counter for drinks and striking the crossbar with a shot.

clue.text: Foul, e.g., no help if team desires hat-trick from him?

indicators.note: foul means fouled up, so these letters are messed into a new order

explanation.surface: A foul, for example, gives no help if the team is after a hat-trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' looks like a football incident but is the anagram signal; a hat-trick of desires is three wishes.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Aladdin tale the spirit summoned from the lamp grants three wishes, a trio like a hat-trick.
